solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Board is liable to be damaged when picked up

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: something liable to be damaged would chip

explanation.surface: A warning about a fragile panel that might get knocked when it is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as lifting the board by hand; here it means caught by ear. Woodchip is board made from compressed chips of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodchip is a kind of board made of bonded wood chips.

clue.text: Extremely old ferries are fitted with propellers

indicators.note: the outer letters carry the other word across, holding it between them
extremely takes the extreme letters of old, its first and last

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Old ferry boats have been fitted with screws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives OD, which 'ferries' ARE in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is oared has oars, which propel it through the water.

clue.text: Really con agent with Dadaist fake (just one time)

indicators.note: a fake is a forged reworking, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: T abbreviates time, and only one of the fodder's two Ts is kept, so one T is surplus

explanation.surface: A con artist uses a forged Dadaist work to deceive an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' is the pros-and-cons word, meaning against, so 'Really con' is strongly opposed. Agent and Dadaist have two Ts; keep just one.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dead against something is to be firmly opposed, and against is what con means in pros and cons.

clue.text: Coastal town contains smart parts

explanation.surface: A seaside town that holds some fashionable districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contains' looks like the container instruction but only supplies HAS; 'parts' does the containing. Hastings is a town on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is a seaside town in East Sussex.

clue.text: Accomplices run to catch up as crossing border

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' sends the letters upward, so they read backwards

parts.note: as = since, as in 'as it's late'

explanation.surface: A fugitive hurrying to catch up with others as they cross a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'up' belongs to R + ENTRAP and turns it into PARTNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Partners in crime are accomplices who act together.

clue.text: Malcontent gambler cleared out with pained expression

indicators.note: the inside of 'gambler' is cleared, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A bitter gambler, bankrupted, wincing at his losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared out' fits a gambler who has lost everything; here it empties the word. A pained expression is something said, not a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name someone chronically dissatisfied and complaining.

clue.text: Fabulous being in possession of European person's make-up

indicators.note: to be in possession of something is to hold it

parts.note: a gnome is a creature of fable

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale creature holding a European's cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests cosmetics; it means constitution, and a genome is the genetic kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A genome is the full genetic make-up of a person or organism.

clue.text: Raising two daughters nothing unusual

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the letters makes them read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: A remark that bringing up two girls is quite ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' reads as bringing up children, which the daughters encourage; it is the upward reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an odd event is out of the ordinary, as in 'that's odd'.

clue.text: Attractive man on board

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a chap
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: A handsome crewman aboard a ship, or a good-looking director on the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' reads as one idiom, aboard ship; split, 'on' just means placed above in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covetable is attractive enough to be wanted.

clue.text: Teetotal workmates eschewing opening spirits

parts.note: a dry person drinks no alcohol
LADS, one's mates at work, without the L

explanation.surface: Colleagues on the wagon turning down the first round of hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' sits beside 'teetotal' as drink; it means supernatural beings. Dryads are tree nymphs of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryads are wood nymphs, nature spirits of Greek myth.

clue.text: Pigeon very casually ignored swallows

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the other letter, as if swallowing it
casually suggests a careless, random order for the letters of ignored

explanation.surface: A pigeon was casually ignored by the swallows, birds in the same scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' looks like birds to go with Pigeon, but it is the containment signal around V.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring dove is the wood pigeon, named for the white patch on its neck.

clue.text: Girl rejected Spandex trousers

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters read in reverse
to trouser is to pocket, so 'Spandex' holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A girl turning down a pair of stretchy Lycra trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is a verb here, pocketing the answer, not the garment the surface puts on the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'girl' in crosswords stands for any female first name, and Edna is one.

clue.text: Nameless boozer masters flayed

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub
DOMINATES with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: An anonymous drunk who has thrashed his employers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' looks like a drinker but is the pub, a common British sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal Latinate synonym, from in- (not) and nomen (name), used of things like the innominate bone.

clue.text: Badly misrepresented yourself in penning article

indicators.note: the rearranged letters pen the article, enclosing it
misrepresented means shown wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer badly misrepresents himself in an article he is writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' looks like it qualifies 'misrepresented', but it is the definition, in the moral sense of wickedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefariously means wickedly or criminally, so it is acting badly in the moral sense.

clue.text: Settler's arrival met with displeasure

parts.note: arr. = arrival, as on a timetable

explanation.surface: A colonist's landing greeted with hostility by the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist; it is one who settles matters, an arranger.
explanation.definitionFit: One who settles or arranges things is an arranger.

clue.text: Vulgar tackling church over singer's morality

parts.note: a tit is a songbird; the 's is ''s' = is, merely linking

explanation.surface: A crude critic taking on the church about a singer's moral standards.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is a bird, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rectitude, from Latin rectus (straight), is upright moral conduct.

clue.text: They're found with keys from bus regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals: every other letter

explanation.surface: Lost property: things that turn up with keys left on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: A fob is the fob on a key ring, often an electronic tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Key fobs are attached to key rings, so fobs are found with keys.

clue.text: Player seems tall on Everton's flanks

indicators.note: the answer runs across the words and ends on Everton's flank, its first letter

explanation.surface: A report that a footballer looks tall playing out wide for Everton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' sits among football words as a footballer; it is an actor, Sylvester Stallone. Everton is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester Stallone is a film actor, a player.

clue.text: Exploratory procedure cut short

indicators.note: cut off the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: SCANT = short, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A medical investigation abandoned before it was finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' is one phrase in the surface; split, 'short' is SCANT and 'cut' docks it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an MRI or ultrasound scan is done to look inside the body and find out what is wrong.

clue.text: Shut away at home, became vocal

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A recluse who stayed indoors and then found a voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Became vocal' reads as speaking up; 'became' is TURNED and 'vocal' says to hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: The interned are confined, shut away, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Establish new radio is faulty

indicators.note: a faulty thing is broken, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that a brand-new radio doesn't work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Establish' reads as proving a fact; here it means to decree or set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of decreeing: laws and rites are ordained, that is, set up by authority.

clue.text: Welcome king hosted by uncomplaining prior

parts.note: a stoic bears hardship without complaint

explanation.surface: A monarch warmly received by a patient monk at his priory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like the monk heading a priory; it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical things belong to an earlier, prior time.

clue.text: As soon as feasible, empty case

parts.note: if a plan is on, it is feasible

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear out a suitcase at the earliest opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As soon as feasible' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'As soon as', as in 'once you arrive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means as soon as: 'once it stops, we go'.

clue.text: Inoffensive note received by family

indicators.note: something received is taken in, as a guest is received into a house

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

explanation.surface: A harmless letter delivered to a household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as a message; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of jokes or language free of obscenity, as in 'keep it clean'.

clue.text: Jaguar groomed with it's tongue

indicators.note: groomed fur is rearranged, so the letters are too

parts.note: used as printed, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A big cat licking its coat clean with its tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe looks like a misprint for 'its'; ''s' is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition. The tongue is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Gujarati is a language of western India, a tongue.

clue.text: Men accepting such charity would be new

indicators.note: if men accepted such a thing inside them, the result would be the word for new, so the answer is what is left when men is taken away from that word

parts.note: maiden means new or first, as in a maiden voyage

explanation.surface: Accepting handouts would be a new experience for these proud men.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: it describes what the answer would make if men took it in, a word for new, so you work back from that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is help given to those in need, so it is charity in the sense of relief.

clue.text: One displaces equestrian in tournament, taking the lead

indicators.note: the lead, or first letter, is taken away

parts.note: a JOUSTER without its first letter

explanation.surface: A knight who unseats a rival in the lists and goes ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the lead' reads as going in front; it removes the lead letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ouster is one who ousts, one who displaces.

clue.text: Dull animal's home beside meadow

parts.note: a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: A boring lair beside a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse of the clue's order: the meadow comes first. Lea is a poetic word for a meadow, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: lead is grey and heavy, so leaden skies or leaden prose are dull.

clue.text: All truly concerning in banks of Europe

indicators.note: the two words go inside the outer letters
the banks of a river are its edges, so the first and last letters of Europe

parts.note: only its outer letters are used
very can mean truly, as in the very thing

explanation.surface: A remark that everything is truly to do with the banks of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks of Europe' suggests financial institutions, but the banks are just the word's two edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone means every person, so it stands for all of the people concerned.
